text:
Ava (support): @channel ACME reports inconsistent embedding shapes from /v1/embeddings across our Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private mix. Same input, sometimes 768-dim, sometimes 512-dim. Also seeing intermittent 401s and a spike in billed embedding units for the same request volume. Customer says it started after we rolled a routing change yesterday. Request id: rwd-req-0a1b2c.
Diego (eng-ml): Do we have the exact request payload and headers? batch_size? model alias?
ACME Support: Here's a minimal repro they gave (redacted keys):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-lucene","input":["How do I reset my password?"],"batch_size":8}'
```
They say running that repeatedly yields different vector lengths ~1/10 runs.
Priya (sre): Noted. Any correlation with region or session token TTL? 401s could indicate token rotation hitting dedicated/private pools without updated creds.
Ava (support): Customer claims they use a single API key and not rotating. They pasted the auth header from a failing request and it looks correct. 401s only appear when dims mismatch occurs.
EmbedOps Bot: alert: routing-change deploy at 1979994000 -> routing policy now uses cost_tier fallback ordering (hosted -> dedicated -> private).
Diego (eng-ml): Hmm. That routing change could route to a dedicated cluster that still has an older model variant pinned (redwood-embed-lucene-v1-512) for cost reasons. If we accidentally fallback to a different model architecture, dims would change.
Joel (billing): The spike — looks like our billing pipeline counted each fallback attempt as a separate embedding call + retry. If client retries on 401, they generate extra billed units. Can confirm if we saw duplicate request IDs?
Priya (sre): I'm pulling request traces for rwd-req-0a1b2c and related ids. Can everyone paste the full X-Request-ID header values when they have them?
ACME Support: Example headers from one failing request:
```
x-request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c
via: routing-hosted, routing-dedicated
```
Ava (support): Customer also attached logs showing server response metadata: 
```json
{"model_returned":"redwood-embed-lucene-v1-512","dims":512,"route":"dedicated-west-1"}
```
and on success: 
```json
{"model_returned":"redwood-embed-lucene-v2-768","dims":768,"route":"hosted-us-east-1"}
```
Diego (eng-ml): That matches variant mismatch. Two things to confirm: 1) Why did routing policy pick the dedicated variant for that key. 2) Why did dedicated still serve v1-512? It should have been onboarded to v2.
Priya (sre): I see spikes in deploy errors during the rollout window; dedicated-west-1 failed model reload due to disk pressure and skipped v2 deployment, leaving v1 pinned. The routing policy fallback doesn't check model version compatibility. Oops.
Ava (support): So steps: tell customer this is why dims change; propose mitigation.
Diego (eng-ml): Short-term mitigation: add a routing filter that enforces model-version-compatibility for embeddings (only route if dims match expected). Medium-term: ensure model pinning for dedicated pools doesn't leave stale variants during rollout.
Joel (billing): For billing: we should refund the duplicate billed units from automatic retry loops. I'll flag invoices and start a credit. Need list of impacted request ids/time range.
ACME Support: Appreciate it. They also asked if batching could produce truncated/padded vectors that look like different dims.
Diego (eng-ml): Batching won't change dims — only model architecture does. Padding would produce identical dims but with zero components, not shorter vectors. So different lengths = different model outputs.
Priya (sre): Action items I'm taking:
- [ ] Collect all traces for requests from 1979993000-1979996000 for ACME API key
- [ ] Temporarily add header-based routing override to pin ACME traffic to hosted until dedicated is healthy
- [ ] Re-run model reload on dedicated-west-1 after freeing disk space
Ava (support): I'll communicate a customer-facing summary and ETA.
Joel (billing): I'll prepare a provisional credit and waive overage while we investigate.
Diego (eng-ml): For repro: I put together a small Python loop that toggles routing and captures returned model meta — can we run it against their key?
```py
import requests
for i in range(40):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings', json={"model":"redwood-embed-lucene","input":["test"],"batch_size":1}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer sk-REDACTED"})
    print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-returned-model'), len(r.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))
```
Priya (sre): Run that from a VM in the same region as the customer and with similar concurrency to mirror routing. Please include the full response headers.
ACME Support: We'll run it tonight and report back. Also they asked: could auth 401s be from an HSM KMS TTL mismatch on private nodes?
Priya (sre): Possible — dedicated/private may have different KMS caches. If a token is validated via KMS and KMS returns an intermittent error, the request can be rejected before routing checks. We'll add KMS error logs to traces.
Ava (support): Next update to customer: explain variant mismatch + temporary pin to hosted + billing credit. ETA 4 hours for pinned routing and reload.
EmbedOps Bot: ticket created: TKT-4682 "ACME embedding dims mismatch - cross-env routing fallout" assigned to eng-ml + eng-sre.
Diego (eng-ml): After patch, we should run a synthetic flood test across hosted/dedicated/private combos with explicit model version checks to ensure no regresses. I'll schedule one after reload.
Priya (sre): Logged the immediate fix: added a version-compatibility gate in the router config (hotfix) and queued reload for 1979999400.
Ava (support): Thanks all. I'll close loop with ACME once the hotfix is live and we credit invoices. :+1:
Joel (billing): Ping me the affected request ids and I'll finalize the credit.
ACME Support: Thanks team. We'll validate tonight and reopen if anything persists.
